This prospective observational study aims to evaluate ocular structural and microvascular changes in adults with obesity who are receiving semaglutide or tirzepatide as part of routine clinical care. Participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus will be included.

Participants will undergo ophthalmologic examinations at baseline and during follow-up. Changes in optic nerve head parameters, retinal thickness, retinal and choroidal microvascular parameters, and choroidal thickness will be

trials.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia. Despite major research efforts, effective treatments that slow or stop disease progression remain limited. Growing evidence suggests that inflammation in the brain and the body plays a key role in the onset and progression of AD. In particular, immune cells called regulatory T cells (Tregs), which normally help control inflammation, are impaired in AD individuals. trials.title: Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Switching From Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RA) to Maridebart Cafraglutide in Adults With Obesity or Overweight (MARITIME-SWITCH)
trials.summary: Efficacy, safety and tolerability of switching from GLP-1RA to maridebart cafraglutide in adults with obesity or overweight.

trials.title: Study of Olatorepatide in Adult Participants Living With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes
trials.summary:
This study will test an experimental drug called olatorepatide ("study drug") to determine how safe and effective this drug is compared to placebo and how easily the body can accept this drug at different doses and dosing schedules without causing side effects, as well as how the drug is processed in the body by participants with overweight or obesity but do not have diabetes.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects the study drug might cause
* How much study drug is in the blood at diffe

trials.title: Somatostatin Analogues vs. Observation After Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy (PRRT) in Nonfunctional Neuroendocrine Neoplasms
trials.summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase III study comparing standard of care use of somatostatin analogues (SSAs) to standard of care observation in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms following treatment with Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy (PRRT) (ethanol-stabilized Lu-177 dotatate).

trials.title: Two-Year Weight Loss With GLP-1 Medications Compared With Sleeve Gastrectomy in Adults With Obesity
trials.summary:
This observational study will compare weight loss over two years in adults receiving GLP-1 receptor agonist medications with weight loss in adults who previously underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, an operation that reduces the size of the stomach.

Adults starting GLP-1 medications as part of their usual care will be followed for 24 months. Their results will be compared with existing medical records of adults who underwent sleeve gastrectomy at the same center. Treatment decisions will

trials.title: A Study to Learn About Switching to a Monthly Study Medicine Called Berobenatide (PF-08653944) to Help Keep Weight Off in People With Overweight or Obesity
trials.summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety and effectiveness of berobenatide in adults with overweight or obesity who have already lost weight while taking semaglutide or tirzepatide. The study does not include people with diabetes.

Participants will be in the study for about 11 months.

trials.title: Postprandial Glycemic and GLP-1 Responses to Modified Full-sugar Drinks
trials.summary: This randomized, double-blind, crossover study will evaluate postprandial blood glucose and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) responses to different sugar-containing beverages in healthy adults. The study will also evaluate whether the addition of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a compound found in green tea, modifies glucose and GLP-1 responses. Participants will complete four study visits and consume a different study beverage at each visit. Blood samples will be collected to measure glucose, G

trials.title: Maridebart Cafraglutide Versus Semaglutide in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes
trials.summary: The main objective of this trial is to evaluate whether maridebart cafraglutide is non-inferior to semaglutide in improving glycemic control in participants with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who are receiving metformin treatment, with or without a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor.

trials.title: A Study to Learn About Study Medicine Called Berobenatide in Adults With Knee Pain and Overweight or Obesity (VESPER-OA 1)
trials.summary: The purpose of this clinical study is to learn about the safety and effects of berobenatide (PF-08653944) for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis in adults with overweight or obesity. The study will last 52 weeks and compare the effects of berobenatide compared to placebo on knee pain, physical function, and body weight. Study activities will include blood tests, knee pain assessment, physical function questionnaires and body measurements.

trials.title: A Study of Orforglipron (LY3502970) Compared With Dulaglutide in Pediatric Participants With Type 2 Diabetes
trials.summary:
This study looks at how well a medicine called orforglipron works compared to another medicine called dulaglutide in pediatric participants aged 10 to less than 18 years with type 2 diabetes. The study will also check how safe these medicines are and how the body processes them.

Participation in the study will last about 61 weeks.

trials.title: Impact of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Analogs on Disease Outcomes in Psoriatic Arthritis: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
trials.summary:
Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory condition that affects the joints but can also have an effect on multiple parts of the body. This study will assess if the effectiveness of Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications used to treat type 2-diabetes and weight management, or nutrition counseling can better treat individuals with Psoriatic Arthritis who are also needing treatment for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

The main objectives it aims to answer are:

To assess disease outcom

trials.title: Effects of Dietary Supplements on Muscle Mass and Function While Using GLP-1 Medication
trials.summary:
This pilot study will examine whether daily protein supplementation with or without a mixture of culinary spices can help preserve muscle mass and function in adults who are using GLP-1 medications for weight management.

The study will include 75 adults who recently started a GLP-1 medication and are experiencing weight loss. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: standard of care, protein supplementation plus placebo capsules, or protein supplementation plus mixed spice

trials.title: A Study to Learn About Berobenatide Given Once Weekly in Adults With Knee Osteoarthritis and Overweight or Obesity With or Without Type 2 Diabetes (VESPER-OA 2)
trials.summary: The purpose of this clinical study is to learn about the safety and effects of berobenatide (PF-08653944) for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis in adults with overweight or obesity with and without type 2 diabetes. The study will last 52 weeks and compare the effects of berobenatide compared to placebo on knee pain, physical function, and body weight. Study activities will include blood tests, knee pain assessment, physical function questionnaires and body measurements.

trials.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) Once Weekly Versus Placebo in Pediatric Participants 6 to Less Than 12 Years of Age Who Have Obesity (ADVANCE-SURMOUNT-KIDS)
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study, performed under Master Protocol J4M-MC-PWMP (NCT06672549), is to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of tirzepatide as an addition to healthy lifestyle in participants 6 to less than 12 years of age, with obesity. Participation in the study will last about 104 weeks.

trials.title: A Study to Investigate the Effectiveness of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) Following Initiation of Ixekizumab (LY2439821) in Participants With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque PsO and Obesity or Overweight in Clinical Practice (TOGETHER AMPLIFY-PsO)
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study is to assess the effectiveness of adding tirzepatide to ixekizumab therapy in standard clinical practice in participants with moderate-to-severe plaque PsO and obesity or overweight with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity.

The study will last up to 12 months.

trials.title: Mirikizumab Administered at the Same Time as Tirzepatide in Adult Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis and Obesity or Overweight: Phase 3b Study
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study is to show whether in these individuals, treatment with both mirikizumab and tirzepatide, compared with treatment with mirikizumab and placebo, leads to decrease or disappearance of UC symptoms, and loss of at least one-tenth of the overall body weight.

Participation in this study will last up to 61 weeks, including 52 weeks of treatment.

trials.title: AI-Assisted Lifestyle Intervention Versus Tirzepatide for Obesity and Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes
trials.summary: This multicenter randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether an AI-assisted intensive lifestyle intervention can improve weight and glycemic management in adults with obesity and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, compared with tirzepatide treatment and standard lifestyle management. Eligible participants will be adults aged 18 to 65 years with a body mass index of 28 to less than 40 kg/m² and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes who have not used glucose-lowering medications in the past 3 months

trials.title: Mirikizumab and Tirzepatide Administered in Adult Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease and Obesity or Overweight
trials.summary:
The main purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mirikizumab and placebo compared with mirikizumab and concomitantly administered tirzepatide in adult participants with moderately to severely active CD and obesity, or overweight.

The maximum duration of this study is up to 61 weeks.

trials.title: A Study to Evaluate LY3537021 for the Treatment of Nausea and Vomiting Caused by Chemotherapy in Adults With Cancer
trials.summary: The purpose of this study is to check how well LY35327021 works and how safe it is for controlling nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy. Participants who join this study will be in it until all parts are finished, which could take about 2 months.

trials.title: A Study of LY3457263 Compared With Placebo in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes on a Stable Dose of Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
trials.summary: The purpose of this study is to measure the change in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) with LY3457263 compared with placebo in participants with type 2 diabetes who are not at HbA1c goal when treated with a stable dose of semaglutide or tirzepatide. Participation in the study will last about 9 months.

trials.title: Semaglutide Dose Effects on Metabolic and Stress Hormone, Craving and Alcohol Use Outcomes
trials.summary: This study will examine two doses of 1.0 mg and 2.0 mg of Semaglutide versus placebo in patients with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) and Obesity (Ob) to assess if these doses improve alcohol craving, stress and alcohol use outcomes.

trials.title: Tirzepatide for Treatment of CCCA
trials.summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn if tirzepatide can treat active central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (CCCA), a type of permanent scarring hair loss, in adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does tirzepatide improve the symptoms and signs of active CCCA?
* Does tirzepatide change the activity of genes in the scalp, especially genes related to scarring?
* Does tirzepatide promote hair regrowth?

Participants will:

* Inject tirzepatide once a week for 12 months

archive.title: ADA: Boehringer touts survodutide weight loss as tolerability questions linger
archive.summary: At ADA 2026, Boehringer Ingelheim presented phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE data for its glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist survodutide, reporting up to 16.6% average weight loss and large visceral-fat reductions. Coverage noted higher treatment-discontinuation rates on the highest doses than for some competing GLP-1 drugs.

archive.title: GLP-1 Drugs 2026: ADA Sessions Close as New Standards End Single-Goal Diabetes Care
archive.summary: A wrap-up of the American Diabetes Association's 2026 Scientific Sessions, where new treatment standards elevated cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction alongside blood-sugar control. The meeting featured phase 3 data for retatrutide, orforglipron and other agents.

archive.title: Ultra-long-acting GLP-1 improves weight loss with and without type 2 diabetes
archive.summary: Data presented at ADA 2026 on berobenatide, an investigational ultra-long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist studied in the VESPER phase 2b program, reported meaningful weight loss in people with obesity or overweight. Its extended half-life points to potential monthly dosing.

archive.title: Rivus Announces Preclinical Data for RV-8451, a Muscle-Preserving Oral GLP-1, at ADA 2026
archive.summary: Rivus Pharmaceuticals reported preclinical results for RV-8451, an experimental oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, describing fat loss with preservation of lean muscle in non-human primate studies. The company said it plans to file an IND application in early 2027.

archive.title: What RFK Jr.'s Peptide Reclassification Actually Means: A Pharmacist's Take
archive.summary: A pharmacist explains the February 2026 HHS announcement that roughly 14 of 19 FDA-restricted peptides would move from Category 2 to Category 1, restoring a legal compounding pathway with a prescription. The article stresses that reclassification is not FDA approval and does not establish safety or efficacy.

archive.title: Novo Nordisk Advances Cardiometabolic Pipeline with CagriSema and Zenagamtide Data at ADA 2026
archive.summary: Novo Nordisk previewed roughly 40 abstracts for ADA 2026, including new CagriSema data on glycemic control and weight loss and mid-stage results for zenagamtide (amycretin). The release outlined the company's broader cardiometabolic pipeline.

archive.title: Next-Gen Weight-Loss Drug Retatrutide Moves a Step Closer to FDA Approval
archive.summary: Eli Lilly's triple-receptor agonist retatrutide, which targets GLP-1, GIP and glucagon, showed participants losing roughly 28% of body weight over 80 weeks in the phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. The results position it as potentially more potent than current single- and dual-agonist obesity drugs.

archive.title: FDA Proposes Ban on Bulk Compounding of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide
archive.summary: The FDA announced on April 30, 2026 that it is proposing to exclude semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list, citing no current clinical need for outsourcing facilities to compound them from bulk substances. A public comment period was opened ahead of a final decision.

archive.title: FDA Mulls Compounding for Peptides Previously Flagged Over Safety Risks
archive.summary: The FDA scheduled a July 2026 advisory-committee meeting to reconsider whether compounding pharmacies may prepare seven peptides the agency had earlier flagged for safety concerns. The piece notes HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s support for broader peptide access.

archive.title: FDA Considers Adding a Dozen Peptides to Its Bulk Drug Compounding List
archive.summary: The Regulatory Affairs Professionals Society reported that the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee will evaluate whether about twelve peptides should be added to the Section 503A bulk drug list for licensed compounding. Proposed indications include wound healing, insomnia and ulcerative colitis.

archive.title: FDA Approves Orforglipron, First GLP-1 Pill Without Time, Food, or Water Restrictions
archive.summary: The FDA approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron (Foundayo), an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, for adults with obesity or overweight, with no food, water or timing restrictions. Trials reported dose-dependent weight loss versus placebo.

archive.title: Tirzepatide Cuts Major Heart and Kidney Risks in New SURPASS-CVOT Data
archive.summary: In the SURPASS-CVOT trial in people with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, tirzepatide met noninferiority versus dulaglutide on the primary cardiovascular endpoint and showed reductions in a broader cardiorenal composite. Gastrointestinal side effects were more common with tirzepatide.

archive.title: Semaglutide Does Not Slow Alzheimer's Disease, Two Clinical Trials Find
archive.summary: Two phase 3 trials (EVOKE and EVOKE+) of about 3,800 patients with early Alzheimer's found that oral semaglutide produced no significant difference in disease progression versus placebo over two years. Some biomarker changes in a subgroup did not translate into slower cognitive decline.

archive.title: Novo Nordisk Expands Pivotal Amycretin Program After Dual Agonist Shines in Diabetes
archive.summary: Novo Nordisk said it would expand the phase 3 program for amycretin, a single-molecule GLP-1/amylin co-agonist, after phase 2 diabetes data showed substantial HbA1c and body-weight reductions. The move advances amycretin alongside the company's CagriSema program.

archive.title: Semaglutide Receives FDA Approval for Treatment of MASH
archive.summary: The FDA approved semaglutide (Wegovy) 2.4 mg as the first GLP-1 receptor agonist for non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis, based on the ESSENCE trial. Reported data showed higher rates of MASH resolution versus placebo.

archive.title: FDA Approval for Mitochondrial Therapeutic Elamipretide, Formerly SS-31
archive.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval to elamipretide (FORZINITY), the mitochondria-targeted peptide previously known as SS-31, for Barth syndrome, a rare mitochondrial disease. The approval was supported by trial data showing improved muscle strength.
